sentence.en: Every grain carries someone’s season of work.

set.name: Shirorekha
set.mechanism: The Devanagari headline that joins letters into one word: a gold line holds three grains in the mark, gives the inscriptional capitals their hanging rule, and is the only gold in a forest-and-ivory palette.
set.expression_move: The gold joining line: the single bright element in mark, layout and pack.
set.differs_by: Category marks are crests, monuments and leaves on maroon or kraft; this is a script-derived abstract mark in deep forest with one line of gold, no illustration.

logo.concept: One line joins three grains into a single word: shirorekha, panicle and toran at once.

misuse.label: Do not join the grains to the line
Never add or remove grains: always three

defaults_used.why: The brief asks for warm ivory, and ivory is the live Sangat site's ground (equity).
The brief asks for a muted gold accent; it is held to one element (line, dot, grain or seal), never a frame or foil flood.

rationale.claim: The Devanagari headline that joins letters into one word: a gold line holds three grains in the mark, gives the inscriptional capitals their hanging rule, and is the only gold in a forest-and-ivory palette.

Category shelf (judgement, sites unreachable here): maroon/red + gold foil with monuments and crowns (India Gate, Daawat, Kohinoor, Lal Qilla), purple/navy script (Tilda), leaf-green kraft and badges (24 Mantra, Organic Tattva).
All faces are OFL Google Fonts designed with both Latin and Devanagari, so Hindi lines use the brand's own type rather than a fallback.
